item.title: Activos financieros argentinos cierran semana en baja
item.description: La plaza financiera de Argentina cerró en terreno negativo y con signos de prudencia el viernes, ante la cautela de inversores institucionales debido a recientes vaivenes del riesgo país y datos macroeconómicos domésticos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La plaza financiera de Argentina cerró en terreno negativo y con signos de prudencia el viernes, ante la cautela de inversores institucionales debido a recientes vaivenes del riesgo país y datos macroeconómicos domésticos. Por su parte, en el contexto externo, las recientes declaraciones del presidente de la Reserva Federal (Fed), Kevin Warsh, generan incertidumbre sobre el devenir de las tasas de interés con impacto en las plazas emergentes. "Warsh pasó por Bangkok y evitó el único tema que el mercado quería escuchar. En una charla con Kristalina Georgieva (...) el presidente de la Fed no dedicó una sola línea a la política monetaria ni al panorama económico estadounidense", dijo Portfolio Personal Inversiones (PPI). Y añadió que "no se adelantó a decir que van a hacer en la reunión de octubre (...). Más allá de esto, el mercado espera con un 85% de probabilidad que mantengan inalterado el rango de tasas en octubre y lo suban recién en diciembre". En el ámbito local, el índice accionario S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires cedió un 0,35% al cierre, mientras que los bonos en el segmento extrabursátil perdieron el 0,1% y cayeron un 0,9% en promedio durante la semana. El riesgo país argentino se afirmaba en la zona de 641 puntos básicos (2000 GMT), luego de oscilar recientemente entre un máximo de 650 unidades a inicios de mes y uno mínimo de 577 registrado la semana pasada como efecto del triunfo electoral de la derecha en Brasil. "Lo mejor que podemos esperar este año (del riesgo país es) que pueda terminar por debajo de los 500 puntos básicos", expresó en una entrevista el economista y docente Martín Polo. Remarcó que pese a los datos negativos de la actividad económica de julio, es "muy probable que los indicadores vengan un poco mejor y el Gobierno se ilusione", lo que podría ayudar a traer inversiones y mejorar el nivel del riesgo país. La tercera economía de América Latina viene de registrar en julio una contracción en su actividad económica (EMAE) de 1,4% interanual y de 2,9% en su medición desestacionalizada. Para agosto, economistas prevén que el EMAE arroje un resultado positivo. El dato oficial de la actividad económica se conocerá a mediados de la semana próxima. El peso argentino mayorista se depreció un 0,3% a 1.518 por dólar para la venta, con el habitual seguimiento de liquidez por parte del banco central (BCRA). La entidad monetaria sumó 68 millones de dólares este viernes y acumuló 642 millones para sus reservas a lo largo de esta semana corta por el feriado del lunes pasado.

item.title: US solicits exchange of up to 17 million barrels of oil from strategic reserve
item.description: The United States has issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States has issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday. The exchange would be part of a global deal [USN:FWN3ZY1GJ TEXT:"the US struck in March"] to try to control fuel prices impacted by the Iran war . Washington agreed then to loan 172 million barrels of oil from the SPR as part of a wider deal with about 30 countries in the International Energy Agency to release 400 million barrels from reserves around the world. The US has released about 132.5 million barrels from the SPR since the US-Iran war began. The latest 17 million barrel round would be a portion of the pending 40 million barrels of oil that would be the last batch of the release. The Department of Energy had offered the 40 million barrels in June, but revealed later that month that companies agreed to borrow only about 500,000 barrels. The government offered those barrels again in late September. While the Department of Energy has not published the awards from that round, Friday's announcement implies that around 23 million barrels were awarded in the September round, research and consultancy Energy Aspects wrote in a note.

item.title: Panzani, Cerealis in talks to create €1.8 billion European food group
item.description: French pasta maker Panzani and Portugal's Cerealis are in exclusive talks to combine their operations in a deal valuing the merged business at about €1.8 billion ($2.03 billion), they said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French pasta maker Panzani and Portugal's Cerealis are in exclusive talks to combine their operations in a deal valuing the merged business at about €1.8 billion ($2.03 billion), they said on Friday. The proposed deal reflects a broader push for consolidation in Europe's food sector as manufacturers seek greater scale to cope with rising costs, strengthen their bargaining power with retailers and expand across regional markets. The deal would create a European food group with about €1 billion in annual revenue and nearly 1,800 employees, the companies said Panzani, which is controlled by private equity firm CVC, generated €620 million of revenue in 2025. Cerealis, controlled by its founding families and Belgian investment company Sofina (SOF.BR) , reported revenue of €400 million Panzani and Cerealis would remain headquartered in Lyon and Porto respectively and retain operational autonomy The merged group would be owned by Cerealis' existing shareholders, including the Moreira da Silva and Silva Domingues families and Sofina, alongside CVC Capital Partners, which would keep a minority stake Cerealis' Executive Vice Chairman Pedro Moreira da Silva would lead the combined group, while Panzani CEO Albert Mathieu would oversee Panzani and its Central European operations. Cerealis CEO Paula Meireles would manage its Iberian and international private-label business ($1 = 0.8887 euros)

item.title: Why is the battle for Yemen's Taiz so important?
item.description: The city of Taiz is rapidly emerging as the most important battlefront in Yemen's reignited civil war, pitting the Iran-allied Houthis against the internationally recognised government, which is backed by a Saudi-led coalition.
item.dc:creator: Angus Mcdowall
item.content:encoded: The city of Taiz is rapidly emerging as the most important battlefront in Yemen's [USN:L6N45S0PX TEXT:"reignited civil war"], pitting the Iran-allied [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"Houthis"] against the internationally recognised government, which is backed by a Saudi-led coalition. Houthi forces have [USN:L1N45Z0S1 TEXT:"encircled Taiz"] in recent weeks by cutting its main road south to Aden, causing widespread displacement and worsening a humanitarian crisis. Here's what you need to know: WHY IS TAIZ SO IMPORTANT? Any Houthi victory in Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, would mark one of the biggest turning points in the country's long civil war, which resumed this summer after a four-year truce. Taiz city has an estimated population of almost 600,000, said Katja Juric, Aden-based head of programmes for the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Government sources said 80,000 had fled in the latest fighting. Taiz has been on the frontline between the Houthis and the government since the first days of the conflict that started in early 2015 and has long been seen as a bastion of opposition to the Iran-allied group. It is the last major urban stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in the southern highland area of Yemen: the rugged hills above both Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based, and the flat coastal plain around the [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb"] Strait. A Houthi takeover of Taiz would make it much harder for government forces to maintain their counterattack around Bab el-Mandeb and keep the Houthis at arm's length from Aden. It would also mean a resounding symbolic defeat for the government and the military coalition of Saudi-backed Yemeni forces fighting the Houthis. WHAT'S THE MILITARY SITUATION AROUND TAIZ? For years the city has sat at the tip of a government salient stretching north into Houthi territory. The Houthis held areas to the north, east and west of Taiz, while government forces had the city and its immediate surroundings including Jebel Sabar, the high mountain rising above it to the south. As fighting in Yemen resumed in recent weeks, the Houthis began making advances to cut off Taiz by seizing territory to the south of Jebel Sabar along the road to Aden, which snakes about 200 km (125 miles) through rugged hills where fighting is slow and difficult. Sections of the road are now under Houthi control, including at the towns of al-Turbah and Mudiriyat al-Misrakh, leaving Taiz encircled since early October, with the Houthis sometimes shelling government positions in and around the city. Government forces, backed by airstrikes from the Saudi-led coalition, are trying to drive the Houthis back from their recent gains and reopen the road, but were still losing ground around Taiz rather than recapturing territory in mid-October. WHY IS TAIZ A STRONGHOLD OF OPPOSITION TO THE HOUTHIS? Taiz had a long history of difficult ties with rulers from north Yemen and was a hotbed of the 2011 Arab Spring uprisings that toppled veteran former president Ali Abdullah Saleh. While the Houthis adhere to the Zaydi school of Shi'ite Islam, Taiz is predominantly Sunni Muslim. Saleh and the Houthis joined forces to seize the capital, Sanaa, in 2014, derailing a political transition that arose out of the Arab Spring and had led to a proposal for a federal, democratic state. In early 2015, army units loyal to Saleh seized positions in the city, leading to big protests there followed by armed clashes. Protesters accused Saleh and the Houthis of mounting a coup d'etat. Months of fierce fighting in and around the city followed, with the Houthis and Saleh's army units battling local fighters and army brigades from Yemen's now fragmented military that backed the government. Taiz citizens endured shelling, sniper fire and terrible shortages in a long siege before government forces eventually drove the Houthis and their allies from the city and re-established a land route to Aden. The fighting in the city lasted throughout 2015 and parts of 2016, and the siege ran for long stretches until 2017. WHAT IS THE HUMANITARIAN SITUATION IN TAIZ? The latest fighting has displaced at least 121,000 in Taiz province, according to the IOM, though many of these are from rural areas outside the city. Inside Taiz, residents have told Reuters about the shortages they now face of basic items and the huge increase in prices they see in the city markets since the Houthis cut the road to Aden. Aid agencies have reported widespread shortages of fuel, food, medicines and clean water. Wheat flour stocks in the city are nearly exhausted, the World Food Programme said in mid-October. The situation risks worsening existing health problems. The UN children's agency UNICEF recently found that one in three of the children it screened in Yemen was malnourished. Cholera, dengue and malaria are all present in Yemen too. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? Government forces backed by Saudi airstrikes are still trying to take back territory to reopen the road, but there is no guarantee they will succeed. The Houthis, who have [USN:L1N46209G TEXT:"upped their attacks"] on Saudi targets while showing themselves [USN:L6N4580DE TEXT:"better armed"] and organised than in earlier phases of the war, are meanwhile trying to cement their siege of Taiz and move closer towards the city. That might lead to a prolonged siege of the kind that Taiz experienced in the earlier phase of the war. It's also possible the Houthis might try to take the city. Local opposition means resistance could be fierce and any such attempt could cause a long, bloody battle.

item.title: Strategy faces MSCI ouster under new rules, billions in passive holdings at risk
item.description: Michael Saylor's Strategy faces potential removal from MSCI's global equity indexes under new rules adopted on Thursday, threatening billions of dollars in passive investment in the bitcoin buyer.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Michael Saylor's Strategy (MSTR.O) faces potential removal from MSCI's global equity indexes under new rules adopted on Thursday, threatening billions of dollars in passive investment in the bitcoin buyer. Shares of Strategy, the world's biggest corporate bitcoin holder and a constituent of the MSCI USA and MSCI World indexes, fell 4.2% on Friday. MSCI said on Thursday non-operating companies will be ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30, as part of its November index review. It will publish the final list of affected companies on November 11. The decision follows a review MSCI [USN:L1N3X907U TEXT:"began "]a year ago, when it proposed excluding digital asset treasury companies on the grounds that they resemble investment funds, which are already barred from its indexes. MSCI [USN:L4N3Y80MJ TEXT:"deferred "]that plan in January and opened a broader review on all non-operating companies. MSCI defines non-operating companies as investment funds and business development companies, and other companies whose finances make them look like one. Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet (3350.T) are on MSCI's list of potential deletions. SharpLink (SBET.O) and several other crypto treasury companies are on a watchlist for possible removal. The changes are aimed at expanding MSCI’s exclusions for passive investment vehicles, with companies required to meet financial tests on their operating assets to remain eligible. Index inclusion matters to companies such as Strategy because passive funds and other investors tracking benchmarks are required to hold their shares. Strategy did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The company warned last year that an exclusion would result in $2.8 billion of its stock being [USN:L6N3XP0XN TEXT:"liquidated "]and would "chill" the industry. Strategy, which pioneered the model of raising money through stock and debt sales to buy bitcoin, had a market value of about $64.3 billion on Friday. Its shares were down 4.8% in 2026.

item.title: TSX rises as oil stocks gain on Brent touching $110 a barrel
item.description: Canada's main stock index gained on Friday, boosted by oil stocks, while investors assessed Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem's warning on persistent energy-price pressures on interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index gained on Friday, boosted by oil stocks, while investors assessed Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem's warning on persistent energy-price pressures on interest rates. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) gained 0.11% to 36,176.55, touching its highest level since September 4. The index gained 1.44% in the week. Energy stocks (.SPTTEN) rose 2.8%. Brent touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May on worries that escalating tensions in the Middle East could further tighten supplies. South of the border, Wall Street ended sharply lower, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure. In Canada, technology stocks <.SPTTTK> fell 3.5%, dragged down by a 5% fall in Shopify (SHOP.TO) and 7.7% decline in BlackBerry (BB.TO) . "It's (AI trade) probably affecting the TSX to a significantly lesser extent than it's affecting some of the US indices... there's a pretty big disparity between tech and everything else at the moment," said Josh Sheluk, CIO at Verecan Capital Management. "The TSX offers a pretty interesting diversifying investment relative to global stocks because it is a lot more heavily allocated and weighted towards not only energy but materials as well," Sheluk said. Macklem said Canada [USN:SPN46200A TEXT:"has not raised interest rates"] yet but the longer elevated energy prices go on "the harder that gets". The BoC is not expected to raise interest rates at its next monetary policy decision announcement on October 28, but money markets are pricing in a rate hike of 25 basis points in December, according to data compiled by LSEG. Data on the day showed that Canadian home sales [USN:L6N46119G TEXT:"extended their decline"] in September, after a drop in August, as higher mortgage rates and expectations of a rate hike weighed on demand.

item.title: Wall Street tumbles as worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
item.description: Wall Street tumbled on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: Wall Street tumbled on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend. The Nasdaq was on track for a loss of over 4% for the week, hammered by concerns that debt-laden AI infrastructure companies may not turn profits in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise. [USN:L6N4620IB TEXT:"Nvidia-backed"] CoreWeave (CRWV.O) slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%. The data center operator's bonds also sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%. Broadcom (AVGO.O) fell 3.6%, and the PHLX chip index (.SOX) sank 2.5%, on track for its eighth straight day of declines. Investors on Friday were also watching oil prices jump more than 3% due to Middle East supply worries. "There is some fear in the market," said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at U.S. Bank Wealth Management in Seattle. "High oil prices, in particular, tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks, and so I think you have investors looking to be cautious into the weekend rather than take more risk." Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611DN TEXT:"are weighing a lower valuation"] for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The S&P 500 was down 1.22% at 7,649.71 points. The Nasdaq declined 2.19% to 26,128.13 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.55% at 51,891.77 points. Six of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by communication services (.SPLRCL) , down 2.52%, followed by a 2.38% loss in information technology (.SPLRCT) . The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since January, and the Nasdaq was heading for its sharpest weekly fall since June. Third-quarter earnings season shifts into gear next week with reports from Tesla (TSLA.O) , Meta Platforms (META.O) and Procter & Gamble (PG.N) . Analysts on average see quarterly earnings surging over 30%, driven by AI-related megacaps, according to LSEG data. While the S&P 500 remains up about 12% in 2026, most of that gain has come from AI-related tech stocks, and the index’s median component has climbed only about 6%, year to date. About 185 S&P 500 stocks have lost ground in 2026. Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week showed price pressures were extending beyond energy commodities. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"voiced optimism"] about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" during a lingering energy shock and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation. Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays [USN:FWN4622T4 TEXT:"now expects"] 25-basis-point hikes each in December and January. Tesla (TSLA.O) dropped 2.5% after the electric-vehicle maker unveiled a [USN:L1N46200L TEXT:"redesigned Roadster"], powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX. Netflix (NFLX.O) [USN:L4N46128P TEXT:"appointed"] former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.9%. Declining stocks outnumbered rising ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 1.3-to-one ratio. The S&P 500 posted 19 new highs and one new low; the Nasdaq recorded 49 new highs and 263 new lows. (This story has been corrected to fix the year to 2026 from 2025, in paragraph 13.)

item.title: Huracán Trudy se debilita frente a costas del Pacífico mexicano
item.description: El huracán Trudy se debilitó el viernes en aguas del Pacífico mexicano, pero podría recobrar fuerzas en las próximas horas, advirtieron meteorólogos, mientras continuaba acercándose a la costa occidental del país, que apenas comienza a recuperarse de una serie de ciclones que han dejado inundaciones y daños en semanas recientes.
item.dc:creator: Diego Oré
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy se debilitó el viernes en aguas del Pacífico mexicano, pero podría recobrar fuerzas en las próximas horas, advirtieron meteorólogos, mientras continuaba acercándose a la costa occidental del país, que apenas comienza a recuperarse de una serie de ciclones que han dejado inundaciones y daños en semanas recientes. A las 14.00 hora local (2000 GMT), el ciclón se ubicaba a unos 365 kilómetros al suroeste de la ciudad portuaria Acapulco, en el estado Guerrero, y sus vientos máximos sostenidos se habían reducido a 140 kilómetros por hora (km/h), mientras avanzaba hacia el norte-noroeste a 7 km/h, según datos del Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC, por su sigla en inglés). "Mientras navegaba por las cálidas y tranquilas aguas del Pacífico oriental, Trudy [USN:L6N46119M TEXT:"se fortaleció rápidamente"] el jueves (pero) perdió algo de intensidad de viento durante el viernes", dijo AccuWeather, una compañía estadounidense de servicios comerciales de pronóstico del tiempo. "Trudy seguirá siendo un huracán peligroso mientras se desplaza cerca de la costa centro-occidental de México durante este fin de semana, con fuertes vientos, mar agitado y lluvias torrenciales", agregó. Más temprano, Trudy llegó a ser un huracán de categoría 3 en la escala de Saffir-Simpson y se esperaba que se intensifique a uno de categoría 4. Un ciclón de ese nivel puede soplar vientos máximos sostenidos de hasta 250 km/h y causar daños generalizados en estructuras protectoras, desplome de tejados en edificios pequeños, erosión de bancales y playas e inundaciones en terrenos interiores. Si bien no se prevé que toque tierra, el ciclón, de categoría 1, descargará lluvias torrenciales y dejará fuertes ráfagas de viento y oleaje peligroso en la franja costera que va desde el conocido destino turístico Acapulco hasta Puerto Vallarta, pasando por los dos mayores puertos del país: Manzanillo y Lázaro Cárdenas, puerta de entrada principal para mercancías provenientes de Asia. La agencia de protección civil de México pidió a los residentes que comenzaran a prepararse para la llegada de la tormenta asegurando puertas y ventanas, y retirando objetos que pudieran ser arrastrados por los fuertes vientos. En Acapulco, una ciudad de unos 700,000 habitantes, los pescadores guardaron sus embarcaciones luego que autoridades cerraron algunos puertos pesqueros y turísticos a la navegación de embarcaciones menores. En las últimas semanas, la costa del Pacífico mexicano ha sido golpeada por los huracanes [USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:"Polo"] y [USN:L8N45V0SM TEXT:"Simon"], y la tormenta Rachel. A causa de las lluvias y las inundaciones, ocho personas perdieron la vida en la ciudad costera de Ensenada, en el estado Baja California. Simon sigue activo, aunque como tormenta tropical, frente a la costa centroccidental del país.

item.title: Russian attacks kill eight in Ukraine, cut power to over a million
item.description: Russian attacks killed at least eight people and injured 60 across Ukraine on Friday, hit two shopping centres and cut power to more than 1 million people after strikes on the energy grid, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian attacks killed at least eight people and injured 60 across Ukraine on Friday, hit two shopping centres and cut power to more than 1 million people after strikes on the energy grid, officials said. A 71-year-old woman and a 58-year-old man died and 12 more people were wounded in attacks on three districts of the eastern city of Kharkiv, Governor Oleh Syniehubov said. He had earlier put the death toll at three. Further Russian strikes through the evening injured nine people, officials said. Attacks in the frontline city of Kramatorsk in Donetsk Region killed two people and two more were killed in southeastern Dnipropetrovsk Region. Ukraine's energy ministry said its repair crews had returned power to over 1 million people who had lost it as a result of Russian attacks on Friday. It was not clear how many were still without power. In the northwestern region of Volyn, which borders Poland, a drone strike on a food-processing facility killed one person and wounded eight others, according to Governor Roman Romaniuk. He said 370,000 people were temporarily without power in the morning, although 100,000 of them got supply back later on. The blackout could last for at least 24 hours in Volyn's regional capital, Lutsk, Mayor Andriy Razumovskyi said on Facebook. Romaniuk said that drone attacks continued throughout the day, striking a customs terminal and torching about 10 trucks in the town of Kovel, which sits on a major trunk road from Kyiv to Poland. Other attacks hit at least two shopping centres — one in the northern city of Sumy, which lies close to the front line, and one in the neighbouring region of Rivne, officials said — the latest in a spate of Russian assaults on malls and markets. Pictures from emergency services in Sumy showed blood spattered across the floor and shots of the centre's damaged entrance. One person was killed and seven wounded by drones that hit a major shopping centre and other sites in Rivne, regional governor Oleksandr Koval said. Ukraine's energy ministry said large parts of the city of Rivne and the surrounding area were without power after attacks on energy infrastructure there.

item.title: Hurricane Trudy weakens but may regain strength off Mexican coast
item.description: Hurricane Trudy weakened on Friday but could regain strength in the coming hours, meteorologists warned, as the storm approached Mexico's western coast, packing winds of up to 140 km per hour (85 mph).
item.dc:creator: Diego Oré, Aida Pelaez-fernandez
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Trudy weakened on Friday but could regain strength in the coming hours, meteorologists warned, as the storm approached Mexico's western coast, packing winds of up to 140 km per hour (85 mph). Further strengthening is forecast before Trudy nears Jalisco and Colima states in central-western Mexico late on Saturday as a life-threatening major hurricane, Mexican authorities and the US-based National Hurricane Center said. The center of Trudy will approach the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico on Saturday and pass near the coast Saturday night into Sunday, the NHC said in its latest advisory. "Trudy will remain a dangerous hurricane as it moves near Mexico's central-western coast this weekend, bringing strong winds, rough seas, and torrential rain," said private forecaster AccuWeather. Earlier, Trudy had reached Category 3 and was expected to intensify to a Category 4 hurricane. Any change in its path closer to shore will increase the severity of its impact, the head of Mexico's weather agency, Fabian Vazquez, said at a press conference. "Everyone in this region needs to be very careful and stay alert over the weekend," he added. Mexico's civil protection agency asked residents to prepare by securing doors and windows, and removing objects that could be thrown around by the strong winds. In the coastal resort city of Acapulco, fishermen pulled their boats ashore after authorities closed some fishing and tourist ports to small vessels. The storm is expected to produce up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, increasing the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, according to the NHC. Mexico's Pacific coast has already been battered in recent weeks by storms that left several dead and caused severe flooding. Tropical Storm Simon continues to weaken farther northwest offshore, after [USN:L1N45Y0H6 TEXT:"dropping heavy rain"] along the coast earlier as a hurricane. Last week, Tropical Storm Rachel hit the Baja California peninsula, damaging some 1,500 homes.

item.title: Wall St Week Ahead As AI rally wobbles, stock market's spotlight turns to earnings
item.description: Stumbles in the market-leading AI trade are set to test investor confidence in the rally in the coming week as Wall Street focuses on quarterly results due from key players including Meta Platforms .
item.dc:creator: Lewis Krauskopf
item.content:encoded: Stumbles in the market-leading AI trade are set to test investor confidence in the rally in the coming week as Wall Street focuses on quarterly results due from key players including Meta Platforms (META.O) . AI-linked stocks, central to [USN:L6N45R12W TEXT:"the bull market"] that just marked its fourth anniversary, [USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"struggled in recent days"], with sharp declines in shares of semiconductor companies and tech hardware firms such as Dell Technologies (DELL.N) . Meta, among the hyperscalers spending massively to build AI data centers, highlights the upcoming week of quarterly reports, along with semiconductor firms Lam Research (LRCX.O) and Texas Instruments (TXN.O) and Elon Musk -led companies SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) . "It certainly feels like the narrative in the market is a little bit jittery," said Garrett Melson, portfolio strategist with Natixis Investment Managers Solutions. "Clearly there's a lot of uncertainty around where AI stands right now." Worries rippled through markets over risks tied to [USN:L6N461185 TEXT:"the financing of the AI build-out boom"], which has lifted profits for a wide swath of companies and boosted economic growth. Investors were watching [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"developments with CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) , an AI cloud company with about $50 billion in debt. This week, its shares tumbled. In other recent signs of caution, strategists at Deutsche Bank and RBC Capital Markets separately pulled back on their recommendations of the tech sector. On October 9, Deutsche Bank strategists said the rotation into tech had "run far and the risk-reward no longer looks favorable in the near term." Dragged down by the swoon in heavyweight tech and AI stocks, the S&P 500 (.SPX) posted its biggest weekly drop since June. But the benchmark index was only about 2% below its record high set this month. Other sectors, which lagged as tech shined last month, posted solid gains on the week, including healthcare and consumer staples. "This is very much an on-off switch type of market," Melson said. "When AI is working, it sucks all the oxygen out of the room for the rest of the sectors." META KICKS OFF HYPERSCALER RESULTS US reporting season heats up next week, with investors counting on robust performance. S&P 500 companies are expected to have increased earnings by more than 30% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES. Massive outlays on AI data centers and infrastructure underpin the profit jump. Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers that combined are expected to increase their capital spending to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs. Investors are eager for signs the companies can show returns on the investments, which would build confidence that the spending is sustainable. "One of the most important takeaways of earnings season is whether or not the profitability of the hyperscalers can grow faster than the pace of their capex," said Kevin Shea, senior equity analyst at BNY Wealth. Shares of Meta, whose market capitalization was about $1.8 trillion, have risen in recent weeks as it launched its Muse AI assistant "With the cost of capital going up, this capex blowout is going to become more expensive, which raises the bar for returns," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services. "Meta is going to be the first up to try to provide some color around that question." SEMIS, TESLA, NETFLIX ALSO ON TAP Chip companies have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the capital spending boom, but the stocks have cooled off. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index (.SOX) has slumped about 12% this month, although it remained up 57% on the year, compared with a roughly 12% year-to-date gain for the S&P 500. Wednesday's reports from Lam Research and Texas Instruments could offer broader indications of demand in the semiconductor industry. Lam Research shares are up 54% in 2026, while Texas Instruments stock is up 59%. Elsewhere, investors will focus on results from Musk-run companies with market values well over $1 trillion: SpaceX — the newly public space company that also has an AI business — and Tesla, another signature stock of the tech-driven bull market. Streaming company Netflix (NFLX.O) , consumer products company Procter & Gamble (PG.N) and engine maker GE Aerospace (GE.N) are among other high-profile reports in the coming week. The rise in Treasury yields and prospects for further rate hikes from the Federal Reserve also remain front-burner issues for stock investors. Hot inflation data this week boosted bets on another rate increase at the Fed's meeting at the end of October. Futures pricing suggested most investors still expect the US central bank to wait until its meeting in December to raise rates for a second time this year. "Another strong earnings season should help equities withstand moderately higher rates," analysts at UBS Global Wealth Management said in a note on Thursday.

item.title: UK clears Axel Springer takeover of Telegraph newspaper group
item.description: Britain's culture minister Lisa Nandy said on Friday she would not refer Axel Springer's planned purchase of the Telegraph Media Group to a more detailed competition investigation, clearing the way for the deal to proceed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's culture minister Lisa Nandy said on Friday she would not refer Axel Springer's [USN:L4N3ZU0XM TEXT:"planned purchase"] of the Telegraph Media Group to a more detailed competition investigation, clearing the way for the deal to proceed. Nandy said the Public Interest Intervention Notice, known as PIIN, issued in January 2024, along with the related public interest merger reference order, had ceased to be in force as a result of her decision. "I will not be referring this matter to a more in-depth 'Phase 2' investigation by the Competition and Markets Authority," she said in a written statement.

item.title: Israeli settlers burn olive trees, injure journalist in West Bank attack
item.description: Clad in black and their faces masked, dozens of militant Israeli settlers burned olive trees and threw rocks at Palestinians in a coordinated attack on Friday on a village's harvest in the Israeli-occupied West Bank that injured at least two people, including a journalist.
item.dc:creator: Pesha Magid, Ali Sawafta
item.content:encoded: Clad in black and their faces masked, dozens of militant Israeli settlers burned olive trees and threw rocks at Palestinians in a coordinated attack on Friday on a village's harvest in the Israeli-occupied West Bank that injured at least two people, including a journalist. Some 80 settlers, some of them carrying gas canisters, descended from a hill above a terraced olive grove where villagers from Abu Falah had gathered to pick ripe fruit, a cherished annual tradition in Palestinian life, Reuters witnesses said. The settlers took positions in front of the terraced lanes of olive trees. Some of them used slings to launch rocks towards Palestinian villagers, who descended towards the bottom of the hill before picking up and throwing stones to defend themselves. "The settlers want to attack us and force us from our homes," said Moutaz Abdelhadi, 42, a farmer who witnessed the attack in Abu Falah. Partway through the attack, at least two Israeli military jeeps sped through the area, kicking up dust as villagers ran out of their way. The attack continued after the military's arrival, with Israeli soldiers firing tear gas in the direction of the Palestinians who had dodged the jeeps. The sound of live gunfire could be heard in the area, and a Reuters photographer saw at least one armed settler fire a gun. In a statement, the Israeli military said soldiers and border police fired what it described as warning shots after deploying to the area and at one point fired towards a person who the troops believed had posed a threat. "Attempts to incite friction between populations undermine security in the area," the military said. "Attacks and violence against innocent civilians are grave and unacceptable," it added. WASHINGTON POST JOURNALIST INJURED Palestinian medics said two people were injured and taken to hospitals in the area of Ramallah. One of them was Heidi Levine, an American photojournalist with the Washington Post. Video of the attack showed Levine lying on her side on a dirt path with her hands over her face as at least three settlers surrounded her. Speaking from a hospital bed later, Levine, who is in stable condition, said: "I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn't even be here, because they just kept kicking me and kicking me." Levine said the attack ended when her Palestinian colleagues intervened, after which medics rushed her in an ambulance to a clinic in Abu Falah and then to hospital in Ramallah. Her voice shook as she spoke, and she had bandages over her left hand. The Washington Post later reported she suffered lacerations across her body and a broken rib, and would need surgery on one hand after a finger was ripped open, exposing bone. In a statement, Matt Murray, the Washington Post's executive editor, called for an investigation into the incident. "This morning, a Washington Post photographer, Heidi Levine, was attacked by Israeli settlers while reporting in the West Bank,” Murray said. "She was wearing visible markings clearly identifying her as a journalist. While we are relieved that Heidi has received medical care and is safe, we are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job and urge a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities." The US State Department said it condemned criminal violence by any party in the West Bank and supported holding the perpetrators accountable. "The Department of State is aware of these reports. We are greatly concerned when any American is harmed overseas and stand ready to provide all appropriate consular assistance," a department spokesperson said. The department has reached out to the Washington Post to offer consular assistance, he added. SETTLER VIOLENCE HAS SURGED IN WEST BANK Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank has surged, with at least 170 attacks since September 27, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli settlements monitoring group. The settlers have been emboldened by the right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has overseen a rapid expansion of settlements and smaller outposts across the West Bank. Netanyahu has criticized the violence but has taken few steps to crack down on incidents that have drawn international condemnation and sanction plans by longtime Israeli allies, including Britain. In a statement, Netanyahu’s office said the incident was under investigation. The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least 3 million Palestinians. UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law regarding military occupations. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied. The Abu Falah attack followed a similar attack on Friday morning in the area of Turmus Ayya village, where settlers burned three cars after attacking a group of farmers harvesting olives. The military did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Salah Abu Niswa, who witnessed the attack in Turmus Ayya, said the settlers "snuck up like thieves, they caught someone by himself and began to beat him."

item.title: Rogue AI agents broke into Indian firms' live systems, government says
item.description: AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, India's cybersecurity agency said, the country's first such official account after similar incidents of rogue AI behavior worldwide.
item.dc:creator: Munsif Vengattil
item.content:encoded: AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, India's cybersecurity agency said, the country's first such official account after similar incidents of rogue AI behavior worldwide. AI model providers had voluntarily disclosed that their agents "exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks" during test runs to access Indian firms' data, including business records, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said late on Thursday. It did not name the providers or the affected organisations. The disclosure brings India into a growing global debate over how AI companies test models with advanced hacking abilities. OpenAI said in July its models [USN:L6N45604D TEXT:"went rogue"] during testing and breached a startup, while Anthropic has disclosed at least four [USN:L4N4511Q1 TEXT:"instances"] of AI models' hacking external systems so far this year. OpenAI has also [USN:L4N45L03J TEXT:"apologised"] for the hacking of an Australian government website by its rogue AI agent. None of the affected Indian entities detected the intrusions themselves, and in every case it was the AI companies that flagged the incidents, CERT-In said. In a second set of cases, the government agency's own investigations found attackers deliberately using freely available AI tools to probe Indian systems and break in for financial gain, with such tools deployed widely across infrastructure in multiple countries. Attacks that once took days from first entry to final damage were compressed to a few hours, CERT-In said, and victims that failed to fully clean up were attacked again within days, at greater depth.

item.title: Stocks slip as dollar heads for weekly loss
item.description: Global stocks fell modestly on Friday as markets stabilized after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss.
item.dc:creator: Chibuike Oguh, Elizabeth Howcroft
item.content:encoded: Global stocks fell modestly on Friday as markets stabilized after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss. Markets have been [USN:L1N46113N TEXT:"rattled"] this week by concerns over higher interest rates and the debt-fuelled financing behind the AI boom, triggering a selloff in technology and chip stocks. Traders increased bets on further US rate hikes after [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"stronger-than-expected"] inflation data was released on Wednesday, while investors piled in to Treasuries and other government bonds. On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq finished down and notched weekly losses. The Dow fell as well after reversing early gains but still scored a weekly gain. Technology and communication services drove losses while the top gainers were utilities and energy stocks. CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) shares shed 12% and lost about 25% this week amid increasing investor scrutiny of the financing for the massive AI infrastructure buildout. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 0.34%, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 1.09%, and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) fell 2.1%. The MSCI World Equity Index lost 0.40% and notched a weekly loss (.MIWD00000PUS) . European stock indexes, [USN:L1N461090 TEXT:"hit less hard"] by Thursday's selloff, gained, with the STOXX 600 adding 0.72% (.STOXX) . London's FTSE 100 (.FTSE) rose 0.38%. Both indexes finished the week higher. "We're starting to see some cracks in the financing of data centers because you're not too sure who's going to be the winners," said Tom Plumb, portfolio manager at Plumb Balanced Fund. "Our view is that there's going to be some really significant winners," he said. "But you have to be careful on the financing capability because companies don't get into trouble because their assets don't exceed their liabilities. They get into trouble when they have liquidity issues." [USN:L1N462067 TEXT:"Asian stocks"] mostly rose, and bond markets steadied, with investors reversing some of the previous session's moves. Indonesian equities suffered their [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"biggest drop since 1998"] after index provider MSCI said the country's market no longer merited emerging-market status and outlined plans to remove it from key indexes tracked by funds. DOLLAR FALLS The dollar index fell 0.26% and was on track for its first weekly decline after four weeks of gains, as lower Treasury yields reduced the currency's appeal. Further worries about AI would push the dollar down further, [USN:L1N46204G TEXT:"analysts said"]. The euro rose from its recent 17-month low. It was last up 0.16% at $1.1238 . The Japanese yen rose 0.01% against the greenback to 157.98 per dollar. European government bond yields edged higher, while US bond yields reversed earlier declines. Germany's 10-year yield rose 1.14 basis points to 3.421% . The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 0.17 basis points to 5.085%. Even so, yields have eased this week as investors sought the safety of government debt amid concerns about AI-related companies' finances. G7 government bond markets were on course for their strongest weekly performance since late May. Brent crude futures rose 3.72% to settle at $109.86 a barrel and were headed for a second straight weekly gain amid concerns over Middle East supplies. Attacks around [USN:L1N46201B TEXT:"the Strait of Hormuz"] have surged in the past 10 days. Gold gained support from the weaker dollar, rising 0.07% to $4,167.14 an ounce.

item.title: Global hedge funds hammered by AI selloff this week, Asia managers lead losses
item.description: Global hedge funds suffered steep losses this week after being battered by the sharp unwind of a swathe of AI bets, with Asia-focused funds hit the hardest.
item.dc:creator: Summer Zhen, Anirban Sen
item.content:encoded: Global hedge funds suffered steep losses this week after being battered by the sharp unwind of a swathe of AI bets, with Asia-focused funds hit the hardest. Investors are increasingly [USN:L1N45Z05C TEXT:"questioning"] whether massive AI spending can [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"pay off"] anytime soon as elevated inflation keeps borrowing costs high. Wall Street ended the week [USN:L6N46212Z TEXT:"sharply lower"] on Friday, with AI-related technology stocks including CoreWeave (CRWV.O) and Broadcom under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend. CoreWeave has been one of the biggest casualties of the latest selloff, with the data center operator's bonds selling off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%. Global fundamental long-short funds, or stock pickers, lost money every single day this week, the Goldman Sachs prime brokerage unit said in a note to clients, with losses for the week to October 15 coming to 2.9%. For the year to date, they have gains of 14.3%. "Following a sharp AI unwind on Wednesday and week-over-week, global equities were net sold again yesterday (Thursday) though at a much slower pace, driven by continued risk unwinds with long sales outpacing short covers. In dollar terms, yesterday's global de-grossing activity — long selling and short covering combined — was roughly half of what we saw on Wednesday," Goldman said in the note on Friday. Goldman added that global AI stocks collectively have been sold by long-short fund managers for six straight sessions. On Thursday, hedge funds across strategies retreated sharply, with stock pickers globally losing 0.9%. Among them, Asia-focused managers were down 2.6%, while tech-focused funds were off 2.0%. Global systematic long-short managers and multi-strategy funds also declined roughly 1%. Hotter-than-expected US inflation data this week that increased expectations of further rate hikes also fueled the selloff in semiconductor and AI supply chain stocks. "From COVID through end-2025, all three broad strategies never fell more than 80 bps on the same day," Goldman Sachs said in an earlier note from Thursday, adding that this has now occurred three times this year, on February 4, July 28 and October 15. Semiconductor-heavy markets bore the brunt of the selloff. South Korea's benchmark KOSPI (.KS11) tumbled 8% to close at a six-month low on Thursday, while Taiwan stocks also lost more than 3%. Asia-focused stock pickers have lost 6.8% for the first half of this month and have erased more than half of the gains from their late-June peak, when they were up more than 40% for the year, according to Goldman Sachs.

item.title: Oil touches $110 a barrel for first time since May on Middle East, Russia supply fears
item.description: Brent touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday on worries that escalating tensions in the Middle East could further tighten supplies, while investors assessed how much diesel Russia could supply to the global market.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: Brent touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday on worries that escalating tensions in the Middle East could further tighten supplies, while investors assessed how much diesel Russia could supply to the global market. Brent crude futures settled $3.94, or 3.7%, higher at $109.86, the highest since May 19, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures closed $3.44, or 3.5%, higher at $101.41, the highest since September 17. So far this week, Brent has risen 4.9% and WTI 10.4%. "WTI and Brent reversed earlier losses as escalation fears resurfaced amid rumours of attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure," research and consultancy Energy Aspects said in a note. " Israeli reports suggest Iran may be preparing a pre-emptive strike following unusual military movements detected by Western intelligence. Although unverified, these developments reinforce our view that persistent escalation risks will keep flat prices supported," Energy Aspects added. A Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched towards the Red Sea city of Yanbu. The port is critical for Saudi Arabia's efforts to bypass the Strait of Hormuz and keep oil flowing to international markets. Initial reports indicated no damage to Yanbu's infrastructure, consultants Rapidan Energy Group said. Supply concerns also increased as attacks around [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"the Strait of Hormuz"] surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. "Intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower," Kpler analysts said in a report on Thursday, adding that they expected a slower and more uneven recovery in Hormuz flows in the absence of a comprehensive political deal. RUSSIA REFINERY ATTACKS Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery on Thursday after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy declared that Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire covering energy sites announced by US President Donald Trump and criticized Trump's willingness to strike deals with Moscow. Russia's Ryazan oil refinery has suspended operations at a primary crude distillation unit following a drone attack in the region on Thursday, two industry sources told Reuters. "Conflict in the Middle East still keeps coming back and I think it's questionable how much diesel fuel Russia can actually deliver to the markets. Those two factors are just continuing to have traders be buyers," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of trading at BOK Financial. To boost supply, the International Energy Agency [USN:L1N4610MY TEXT:"agreed"] on Thursday to release more than 20 million barrels of fuel to the market. The United States also issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday. Washington previously agreed to loan 172 million barrels of oil from the SPR as part of a wider deal with about 30 countries in the International Energy Agency to release 400 million barrels from reserves around the world. Brent crude was little changed on Thursday, while WTI settled up more than 3% after news that the US was weighing plans to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers and after a big [USN:L6N46115T TEXT:"US crude stock draw"] on hurricane production shut-ins.

item.content:encoded: Wall Street termine en nette baisse, plombée par l'IA et le pétrole 16 octobre (Reuters) - La Bourse de New York a fini en nette baisse vendredi, encore une fois plombée par les inquiétudes entourant l'endettement des entreprises du secteur de l'intelligence artificielle, mais aussi par une nouvelle hausse des prix du pétrole.   L'Europe finit dans le vert, la "tech" pénalise à nouveau le Nasdaq 16 octobre (Reuters) - Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en hausse vendredi et sur de solides gains hebdomadaires, les indices du Vieux Continent restant largement épargnés par les craintes sur le secteur technologique qui secouent à nouveau Wall Street, et renouent avec un peu de sérénité grâce à la baisse des rendements obligataires. UniCredit autorisé par la BCE à prendre le contrôle de Commerzbank MILAN, 15 octobre (Reuters) - UniCredit a obtenu l'autorisation de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) pour prendre le contrôle de Commerzbank, a annoncé jeudi soir la banque italienne, alors que son offre publique d'achat hostile a porté sa participation dans son concurrent allemand à 48%. Schneider relève ses objectifs 2026 après un T3 record porté par les centres de données 16 octobre (Reuters) - Schneider Electric a relevé vendredi pour la deuxième fois de l’année ses objectifs de résultat d'exploitation et de chiffre d’affaires 2026, porté par la demande des géants du cloud pour les centres de données dédiés à l’intelligence artificielle. Christine Lagarde pourrait être nommée présidente du Forum de Davos dès novembre-sources Le Forum économique mondial (WEF) pourrait nommer Christine Lagarde à sa présidence dès novembre, ont déclaré à Reuters quatre sources proches de l'organisation, ce qui impliquerait un départ anticipé de ses fonctions à la tête de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE). L’AIE va accélérer la mise sur le marché des stocks de pétrole, dont plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel L’Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est convenue jeudi de mettre sur le marché plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel dès que possible, ainsi que les volumes restants des réserves d’urgence libérées en mars, afin de contribuer à approvisionner le marché et à freiner la flambée des prix. États-Unis: Les prix à la production enregistrent en septembre leur plus forte hausse en quatre ans et demi Les prix à la production (PPI) aux États-Unis ont enregistré en septembre leur plus forte hausse en quatre ans et demi, sous l'effet de l'augmentation des coûts des biens et des services, dernier signe en date d'un élargissement des pressions inflationnistes au-delà des produits énergétiques.

item.content:encoded: L'Iran exporte du GPL et du kérosène malgré le blocus américain, selon des données DAMAS/LONDRES, 16 octobre (Reuters) - L’Iran a réussi à exporter quelques cargaisons de gaz de pétrole liquéfié (GPL) et de kérosène depuis juillet, malgré le blocus naval américain, selon des données de suivi du trafic maritime et des sources spécialisées dans la sécurité. L'Ukraine dispose de réserves de gaz au plus haut niveau depuis 2020, selon le DG de Naftogaz KYIV, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Le directeur général par intérim de Naftogaz, la société publique ukrainienne du pétrole et du gaz, a dit à Reuters que l'entreprise avait constitué ses plus importantes réserves de gaz depuis six ans en prévision de l'hiver, malgré une recrudescence des frappes russes sur ses installations. Zelensky dénonce la "parodie" diplomatique de Moscou, fustige les expédients de Trump BRUXELLES/KYIV, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Volodimir Zelensky a durci le ton vendredi à l'égard de la Russie, accusée de feindre une "parodie" de processus de paix, et visé par ricochet Donald Trump auquel il reproche de "remplir les poches" de Vladimir Poutine pour poursuivre la guerre en Ukraine. La Chine est prête à coopérer avec l'UE pour remédier aux déséquilibres mondiaux PÉKIN, 16 octobre (Reuters) - La Chine est prête à engager un dialogue avec l'Union européenne (UE) pour améliorer la communication sur certains aspects de la gouvernance économique mondiale et de la coordination des politiques macroéconomiques, a déclaré vendredi le ministre chinois des Finances.
